A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TKG-DM work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v2 ends after its references; v3 additionally includes supplementary Sections 9–11 and Figures 12–32. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments using 3,000 MAGICK examples, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–2, and a 100-participant user study in Figure 8.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds parameter studies, generation diagnostics, and qualitative application results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The channel-mean shift and Gaussian noise blending in Section 3 remain unchanged. Section 11.1 adds a limited inference adaptation through Multi-Diffusion: applying TKG-DM centrally while using ordinary noise elsewhere. FLUX experiments reuse the existing shift technique.

E1.justification: Section 11 and Figure 32 add exploratory Multi-Diffusion regional compositions and SV3D multi-view examples. The text-to-3D pipeline is explicitly incomplete. MAGICK and the existing image-generation, ControlNet, layout, consistency-model, and video coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The new denoising and guidance comparisons explicitly include ordinary SDXL without GBP alongside SDXL+GBP and TKG-DM, expanding the diagnostic controls in Figures 16–24. The main benchmark and user-study comparator sets remain unchanged; FLUX and SV3D are application models, not new competitive baselines.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings remain unchanged. The supplement substantially expands evaluation protocols with displayed shift settings from 0% to 14%, denoising budgets from 1 to 50, intermediate outputs within a 50-step run, guidance scales from 1 to 10, and negative-prompt controls. It also adds FLUX-based evaluation.

E4.justification: Section 9 extends the original channel and attention illustrations with shift-strength sensitivity, denoising-budget and trajectory analyses, guidance-scale robustness, and negative-prompt color and size-control cases. Figures 12–25 provide substantial new diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its results. The supplementary image grids introduce no new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the Figure 8 user-study results are unchanged. The supplement substantially expands qualitative findings: background uniformity near the illustrated 7% shift setting, foreground degradation at stronger shifts, early denoising behavior, guidance stability, and negative-prompt effects. It also adds FLUX and application outputs.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3, the positive-ratio definition, channel-shift construction, and Gaussian blending remain unchanged. The supplement adds empirical observations and explanations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free chroma-key generation, foreground control, versatility, and competitiveness with fine-tuned models. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The supplement substantially expands interpretation through the background-uniformity versus foreground-alignment trade-off, explanations of guidance and negative-prompt independence, and architecture-generality arguments based on FLUX. It also explicitly qualifies the text-to-3D application as incomplete. Section 7's original limitations remain.

D1.justification: Sections 10.3–11 document frozen FLUX parameters, model-specific channel/color relationships, regional noise handling for Multi-Diffusion, and SV3D integration. These provide limited additional implementation guidance; the original benchmark setup and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 56 to 63 references, adding MultiDiffusion, Flow Matching, LayerFusion, LayerDiff, ALFIE, Text2Layer, and zero-shot subject-centric generation. Related-work citation coverage broadens, but the substantive positioning against MAGICK and LayerDiffuse remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 1–8 remain essentially verbatim and in the same order. v3 adds a separately organized supplement with explanatory subsections and captions, without extensive rewriting of the existing narrative. Some new figure cross-references are incorrect, including those in Sections 9.2 and 10.2.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 12–32, including parameter-sweep montages, denoising trajectories, prompt-control comparisons, and model/application galleries. This substantially expands the visual presentation. The original Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–2 retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: The supplement makes parameter sensitivity and failure behavior inspectable, especially the loss of foreground alignment at stronger shifts, and supplies application evidence referenced but absent in v2. This improves transparency and practical understanding. The gain is bounded by predominantly illustrative evidence and incomplete 3D integration, while incorrect supplementary figure references slightly reduce clarity.
